title: The else is the leftover bucket
idea: else at the end of a chain catches every case no branch above matched. Decide what belongs in that catch-all. Thinking.

exercises.prompt: In if / elif / else, the final else runs when...
options: none of the earlier tests were True
exercises.explanation: else is the leftover bucket: it only runs if all the branches above it were False.
0 is not > 0 and not < 0, so the else catches it: 'Zero'. The leftover bucket handles the exact-zero case.
7 > 0 is True, so 'Positive' prints first and the rest is skipped.

exercises.prompt: Leaving off the else is allowed, but then nothing runs when no branch matches.
exercises.explanation: Right - without else, an unmatched value simply produces no output. Add else when you want a guaranteed result.

exercises.prompt: Why is it risky to forget the else in a classifier?
options: Some inputs may silently produce no result
exercises.explanation: Without a catch-all, surprising inputs fall through with no message - a quiet bug that is easy to miss.

exercises.prompt: Match each positive/negative/zero chain outcome to its input.
exercises.explanation: Positive and Negative are caught by the if and elif; zero falls through to the else bucket.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the catch-all keyword:

if n > 0:
    print("Positive")
elif n < 0:
    print("Negative")
____:
    print("Zero")
exercises.explanation: else is the leftover bucket. Here it catches the only remaining case: exactly zero.

exercises.prompt: A chain sorts a weekday number into Mon/Tue/Wed... with no else. For an unexpected 9, what happens?
exercises.explanation: 9 matches no branch and there is no else, so nothing prints. An else saying 'Not a weekday' would be safer.

exercises.prompt: Adding an else like 'Unknown' can turn a silent miss into a helpful message.
exercises.explanation: Yes - a catch-all else gives surprising inputs a clear response instead of silence.

options: it is the catch-all for everything the branches above missed
exercises.explanation: else sweeps up every leftover case. Decide on purpose what that bucket should say.
